carla_cust: Hey team — our users started seeing OAuth failures this morning on Android builds.
carla_cust: After Google login, app lands on our callback and shows "invalid_request". No code param.
alice_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the full callback URL you see, and the client_id+redirect_uri you're using?
carla_cust: Here's the exact redirect we get from the device:
carla_cust: myapp://auth/callback#access_denied&error_description=redirect_uri%20mismatch
carla_cust: Our redirect_uri registered is https://auth.example.com/mobile/callback
alice_support: Hmm — I see a fragment (#) being returned from the provider instead of query params. Are you using implicit or code flow with PKCE?
carla_cust: We're using Authorization Code + PKCE (mobile client). It works on web; only Android fails.
bob_eng: Can you grab app logs around the redirect? Specifically the incoming deep link handler and the query string parsing.
carla_cust: Pasted from device log:
carla_cust: 2024-05-05T09:12:03.123Z Incoming intent: action=VIEW data="myapp://auth/callback#code=4/ABCD...&state=xyz123"
carla_cust: Then our handler extracts the query params but gets empty code.
dan_mobile: Likely the Android browser or intermediate redirect is turning the code into a fragment — some webviews do that when using POST or if redirect contains a hash. Also check if intermediate CDN/proxy rewrites URLs.
alice_support: @bob_eng any chance our callback endpoint expects code in query and drops fragments? If app receives fragment, it must parse after '#'.
bob_eng: Right — server endpoints don't get fragments (they're client-side). If the provider returns #code=..., that's intended for implicit flow (token via fragment). With PKCE you must get code in query (?code=...). If Google returned a fragment it's usually because the redirect_uri uses a custom scheme and OAuth client config flagged 'use fragment'.
bob_eng: Also check code_verifier length: we've seen some mobile redirectors truncate long verifiers and cause invalid_grant or mismatch.
carla_cust: Error we see in backend logs:
carla_cust: 2024-05-05T09:12:04Z POST /oauth/token 400 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"code_verifier mismatch"}
alice_support: That points to PKCE verifier mismatch, not missing code. But earlier you said no code param — confusing. Could there be two different code paths?
carla_cust: I think browser returns fragment to app; app extracts code and sends token request, then server rejects with invalid_grant.
dan_mobile: On Android, some intent filters drop the fragment. Make sure your activity reads getDataString() and also getData() then call getFragment(). Also check if a proxy (like analytic redirect) encodes '#' as '%23' which changes behavior.
bob_eng: Can you reproduce with adb? Run:
bob_eng: adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "myapp://auth/callback#code=TESTCODE&state=xyz123" com.example.app
carla_cust: Tried that — app shows code in logs. After exchange we still get invalid_grant.
alice_support: Please share the token exchange request (redact secrets): headers, body (grant_type, code, redirect_uri, code_verifier).
carla_cust: Body we send:
carla_cust: grant_type=authorization_code&code=TESTCODE&redirect_uri=https://auth.example.com/mobile/callback&client_id=mobile-client&code_verifier=verylongverifierstring...
carla_cust: Token endpoint responds invalid_grant.
bob_eng: Two common causes: 1) redirect_uri doesn't exactly match registered redirect (trailing slash, scheme mismatch), 2) code_verifier doesn't match original code_challenge used in auth request (maybe we trimmed it client-side).
bob_eng: Did your initial /authorize request include S256 code_challenge? If code_challenge method is plain vs S256 mismatch will fail.
carla_cust: Our authorize request uses code_challenge=Sjk...&code_challenge_method=S256
carla_cust: I checked mobile's stored code_verifier; it's 128 chars. But the token exchange shows only first 64 chars sent — looks like our networking library truncated body parameters.
dan_mobile: Aha — some mobile HTTP libs restrict form field length when using application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or encoding mishap with multibyte chars.
alice_support: Also verify redirect_uri exactness: you said registered redirect is https://auth.example.com/mobile/callback (no trailing slash) — make sure request uses same string.
carla_cust: Confirmed redirect_uri matches. Fixing the truncated code_verifier in mobile SDK reproduces success in local testing.
carla_cust: After fix: token exchange returns 200 with access_token.
alice_support: Great. For production mitigation: can we add server-side fallback to better error logs (log incoming code length), and add a user-friendly error to surface 'Try updating app to latest' instead of opaque invalid_grant?
bob_eng: I'll add a telemetry rule to log code length and code_verifier length when invalid_grant occurs and include a correlation id.
deploy-bot: deploy started: feature/oauth-codeverifier-length-telemetry -> staging
alice_support: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups:
alice_support: - @dan_mobile please ship the mobile patch (short-term workaround: validate verifier before send)
alice_support: - @bob_eng add telemetry and a KB note for support
alice_support: Closing once fix is in prod. :thumbsup:
carla_cust: Thanks, deploying patch now, will update if anything else pops up.
